title: We can afford a RM700,000 landed home at 30. Should we buy it now?
excerpt: A couple of 30 renting in KL weigh a subsale terrace in Elmina against a new launch nearby. Sean says either works, but he would buy neither until they need it.

question.asker: From V, a viewer who wrote in by email
question.context: V and his partner are both 30, in white-collar jobs, with a joint income of about RM15,000 a month. They rent a unit in KL for RM2,000 and work from the office only one or two days a week. They are looking at a RM700,000 subsale landed home in Elmina Green, or a pricier new launch nearby, so they can start a family in one to two years. They already own a subsidised apartment in PJ.
question.text: Should they buy the landed home now before prices rise, keep renting, or pick the new launch instead?

answer.quote: I would buy neither because I don't need it yet.
answer.summary: They can afford either, and the subsale is the better value, so it comes down to how much they want to pay for the dream. Sean himself would buy neither yet: he would use the loan on an investment unit that earns rent, and buy the dream home only when it is actually needed.

reasons.title: The fear is about your own income
reasons.body: Worrying that you won't afford a home later really means doubting your future earnings. At 30, their best earning years, roughly 35 to 45, are still ahead, so this is the time to build momentum.

reasons.title: Renting is only wasted if it isn't working for you
reasons.body: Rent pays for being close to work. If they rarely go to the office, a RM700,000 subsale on a 90% loan costs about RM3,000 a month, only about RM1,000 more than their rent.

reasons.title: Subsale for value, new launch for timing
reasons.body: The subsale is better value for money. A new launch costs more and its keys may be about two and a half years away, so they should check that the timing suits their family plans. Being closer to the township's centre helps capital appreciation, but a mall nearby can also bring congestion.

reasons.title: A dream home uses up the slot and the savings
reasons.body: After buying, they would need years to rebuild their savings and could miss other opportunities. Sean would instead use the 90% loan on an investment apartment that can be rented out or lived in, and repeat.

actions: Decide whether this home is meant to be the last one, or whether you want to keep building wealth first.
Compare the instalment on a 90% loan with the rent you pay now.
For a new launch, check when the keys will be handed over and whether that suits your plans for a family.
Weigh distance to the park, highway, shops and mall against the price.
Make sure any savings you keep are doing more than sitting in a savings account.
caveat: There is no right or wrong here. If they see this as their home for life and are happy raising a family there, buying it within their means is fine; Sean's own choice reflects his risk appetite and ambition, not a rule for everyone.
sourceNote: Summarised from Sean's full English captions for Asking Sean #208. The quoted line is verbatim; everything else is paraphrased. Figures are as the viewer and Sean stated them in March 2023, when a 90% loan was available to them; loan rates and prices have changed since.
